title: How to Choose What to Study
summary: A practical way to think about subjects, strengths and careers without panic.

steps.title: Start with three questions
sentences: Ask what you enjoy doing, what you are good at, and what the world needs.
Where these overlap is a good place to look.
You do not need a final answer now.

steps.title: Know the fields
sentences: Broadly, fields include science and technology, medicine and health, commerce and business, law and public service, arts and design, and skilled trades.
Each has many different jobs inside it.
For example, a person in science might become a researcher, a teacher or a data analyst.

steps.title: Try before you decide
sentences: Join clubs, do small projects, talk to people who do the work and watch good online lectures.
Even a short try tells you if you like the daily reality of a job.
Notice what you lose track of time doing.

steps.title: Keep doors open
sentences: Strong basics in maths, reading, writing and clear thinking help in almost every career.
Skills like teamwork and learning new things are valuable everywhere.
Many people change careers, so choose for now and keep learning.

facts: Many of today's jobs did not exist twenty years ago, such as social media manager and app developer.
Entrance exams and course options in India change from time to time, so check official sources for the latest rules.
Skilled trades like electrician and chef offer good careers too.

quiz.q: Which question helps choose a field?
options: What do I enjoy and do well?
quiz.why: Interests and strengths are a good start.

options: To learn what the work is really like
quiz.why: Trying shows the daily reality of a field.

quiz.q: Which skills help in almost every career?
options: Reading, writing, maths and clear thinking

notes: Exam and admission rules change; confirm with official sources.
